environment: Fly Sprites; local workerd; isolated local Postgres; fake providers
behaviorDifferences: The two Postgres recovery fault-injection cases remain failures: Workers uses Durable Object journals, not versioned Postgres runtime headers or pending_runs. A comparable Durable Object recovery/fault-injection contract remains to be implemented.

Deployed account mail uses Cloudflare EMAIL. The local fixture sends the source SES envelope to MAIL_TEST_URL. SES configuration sets/tags and signed SNS bounce/complaint feedback are not implemented for the deployed Cloudflare transport.

Deployed outbox, deletion and other maintenance retries use the existing five-minute Cron instead of the Node process pollers. Mutating account routes start mail delivery immediately. Local mail fixtures drive the real scheduled handler every second. The local fixture uses waitUntil, coalesces overlapping tenant reloads, and retries transient closed connections up to three attempts; it retains no settled configuration cache.

Account deletion retains the source ledger, payment and anti-abuse SQL and explicitly purges active Durable Object/R2 data after pending settlements. Export adapts history/configuration/schedules to Durable Objects. Cloudflare retained backups/PITR are outside the tested active-data purge; configured Journey store data is included in export and source Journey SQL erasure is retained; out-of-scope channel data has no Workers adapter. Ordinary agent deletion/expiry still retains the revoked Durable Object journal until account-level purge; this change does not add the Node general revoked-agent purge sweep.

Admin Access authorization and statistics work, but the existing Workers admin API omits channel/voice and ECS diagnostics; admin static pages and report-store serving remain absent. The console shell is available only when ASSETS is bound. Invalid admin email allowlist entries and a pathless admin URL equal to the runtime hostname are not rejected at startup; the source admin read queue bound and per-tab audit names are also not implemented.

Native file quotas count retained R2 file bodies plus source storage_usage totals. Native files do not have source content-addressed deduplication or volume-metadata accounting; their bytes are not yet fed into the daily source storage-billing meter. Quota reads list the tenant R2 prefix.

Event subscriber counters are Worker-isolate local, comparable to Node process-local counters. The current WebSocket wrapper releases its subscriber slot at the 101 response, so a long-lived negotiated agent-token WebSocket does not retain that cap; SSE and polling are covered.

Creation reservations expire after 60 seconds in the Tenant Durable Object. Busy-limit refusals currently use the Workers generic message instead of the source tier-specific explanation and busyAgents detail object.

The limits response uses the Workers decision-concurrency bound of 64; its decider does not consume AGENT_DECISION_NODE_CONCURRENCY. Provider gateway checks perform DNS preflight but Workers fetch does not pin the checked DNS result.

Active time is settled through immutable per-request receipts at completion, whereas Node also flushes active time once a minute. Rounding occurs per receipt instead of the Node flush batch. Host execution starts its timer after admission/preparation; periodic live active-time billing remains a separate parity gap.

Builtin web usage is posted with its auxiliary idempotency receipt, tenant debit and end-user debit in one transaction before the tool returns; Node queues the end-user debit asynchronously with retry. Source allowance, markup, lot-expiry and write-off rules are reused unchanged.

During a PostgreSQL outage, first terminal publication can precede retrying a durable billing receipt or releasing its busy slot. Completed-record reads explicitly retry settlement. The receipt remains replay-safe; completion and ledger visibility are not a single distributed transaction.
